body:
Independent fresh-context review of the exact head `e6053f11e07e39de66d97874eef1ce730622b1f1`, by two models of different families, each in a fresh read-only context that did not author the change.

**Verdict: APPROVE — no P0 findings, no P1 findings.**

What the review verified:

- A burst of fifty callers against a healthy but slow upstream causes **one** upstream call, and every caller is answered with the catalogue. The opposite mutation, a lock that never gives way, fails two tests.
- The last good catalogue is kept when the upstream answers with a shape the gateway cannot read: an entry that is not an object, an entry with no identifier, a `models` that is absent, null or not a list. The catalogue recovers as soon as the upstream does.
- A failure is never cached as an empty catalogue. A catalogue that really holds no models is, and the endpoints answer `503 catalog_unavailable` when no catalogue was ever read.
- The endpoints answer `503 catalog_unavailable` on `/v1/models`, on `/v1/images/generations` and on the image path of the chat endpoint while the upstream is down, and a chat request without an image still works.

The reviews drove three rounds of fixes, each with a regression test that fails against the pre-change code: a response the gateway could not read was taken for a catalogue that holds no models and replaced the last good one; a catalogue that was fetched and holds no models was never cached, so every request asked the upstream again; and the wait of a caller that has no copy was not held by any test.

Two things are stated in the changelog and the README rather than hidden: the images of a request share the catalogue of the request, and a catalogue whose entries the gateway cannot read is a failure, so the last catalogue that was read is served instead.

The `CI` and `dco` checks are green on this head.
